title: EXCLUSIVE: State Department accuses politicians of endangering Afrikaner lives after gruesome farm attacks
summary: The State Department accused South African politicians of endangering Afrikaners' lives after a farmer was allegedly tortured and a woman beaten to death.
story: Anti-migrant protests take a violent turn in South Africa, as unrest spreads and the government pleads for calm.

FIRST ON FOX: The State Department has hit out strongly against South Africa and some of its politicians, accusing them of putting their people’s lives at risk after two attacks on White farmers believed to be Afrikaners — people of European descent — near Johannesburg.
A 50-year-old man was reportedly tortured, and a 55-year-old woman was allegedly beaten to death.
In exclusive comments to Fox News Digital, a State Department spokesperson said "the lives and property of Afrikaners have been endangered by politicians who incite race-based violence against them."

President Donald Trump, right, and Cyril Ramaphosa, South Africa's president, during a meeting in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, D.C., May 21, 2025. (Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
BIDEN-ERA DIRECTIVE FOR DIPLOMATS TO PEDDLE DEI ON FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS SCRAPPED BY STATE DEPARTMENT

This is the latest volley from the administration in an increasingly bitter row, which first burst out of the Oval Office last year in a heated exchange between President Donald Trump and South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa on a range of the country’s policies and issues, including safety concerns for the Afrikaner community.
"This month’s attacks were appalling," said Ian Cameron, chair of South Africa’s Portfolio Committee on Police and a member of Parliament with the main opposition Democratic Alliance.
He detailed the attacks, starting with one involving Donovan Marx, a 50-year-old who was on his farm about 80 miles from Johannesburg.
Cameron told Fox News Digital there were reports Marx was shot, stabbed and had his ears cut off, describing the attack as "extraordinary cruelty."
He added that, in a separate attack in the same North West Province earlier this month, a female farmer, Hannetjie van Zyl, 55, was beaten to death while opening a gate.
President Donald Trump shows documents as he meets South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa at the White House May 21 in Washington. (AP/Evan Vucci)
Eyewitness reports claim she was approached from behind and hit repeatedly over the head with an iron bar.

In both attacks, the victims’ vehicles and belongings were reportedly stolen. But the alleged torture of Marx goes beyond straightforward crimes such as burglary, Corné Mulder, leader of the opposition party Freedom Front Plus, told Fox News Digital.

"Safety and farm attacks in South Africa remains a huge problem," Mulder said. "Donovan Marx was attacked this week. He's fighting for his life in hospital at the moment. The perpetrators not only attacked him, they tried to castrate him."
While both victims were White, there have been no accusations from public figures that the attacks were racially motivated.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa delivers the State of the Nation address in Cape Town, South Africa, Feb. 12, 2026. (Rodger Bosch/Pool via Reuters)

Cameron claimed the attacks were not isolated, noting he had "personally attended farm attack scenes in which people were tortured with boiling water, burnt with clothing irons and subjected to other horrific abuse."

"SAPS [South African Police Service] must put experienced investigators, forensic support and crime intelligence behind these cases," Cameron said. "Nobody should have to accept this level of violence as a normal part of life."

The reported torture of farmers is "unthinkable," Mulder said, adding "not one word from the President of South Africa to sympathize, not even acknowledging that this has happened, which is absolutely unbelievable."
"We have been pleading with [the] government to prioritize rural crime and farm attacks as a priority crime, they are not prepared to do so," he continued.
Fox News Digital reached out to the South African government for comment but was referred to police, who did not immediately respond.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa addresses the opening session of the G20 leaders' summit in Johannesburg, South Africa, Nov. 22, 2025. (Misper Apawu/ AP Phot/Pool)
SOUTH AFRICAN EX-POLICE CHIEF GETS TISSUE STUCK ON FOREHEAD WHILE SWEATING DURING CORRUPTION INQUIRY

Mulder claims the recent farm attacks were fueled by the South African president’s refusal to heed Trump’s demand last year to stop performances of the song "Kill the Boer, Kill the Farmer." The term "Boer" refers to a South African of Dutch or Huguenot descent, according to Merriam-Webster.
Ramaphosa said he could not stop the song being chanted in stadiums by crowds of up to 90,000 because the country’s highest court has said the lyrics are not hate speech.
THOUSANDS OF POLICE DEPLOYED ACROSS SOUTH AFRICA AS DEADLY ANTI-IMMIGRATION PROTESTS SPREAD TO MULTIPLE CITIES

"As long as [President Ramaphosa] does not stop the incitement to attack farmers with the singing of the song ‘Kill the Boer,’ the attacks will continue," Mulder wrote in a statement. "We see the practical reality when these things play out as happened with the last two farm attacks that we've seen."
Last month, U.S. Ambassador to South Africa Brent Bozell III told Fox News Digital Ramaphosa could ban the song despite a court ruling that it did not constitute hate speech.
"So, to say, ‘Well, you can’t do it because the court said it’s not,’ … you know, that’s poppycock," Bozell said. "If President Ramaphosa, if he wants to, he can do it. It’s just as simple as that."

The State Department doubled down on the administration’s demand that the singing of the song be banned, with a spokesperson telling Fox News Digital on Friday, "The United States asked senior government officials to condemn incitement to race-based violence, particularly the singing of "Kill the Farmer! Kill the Boer!"

U.S. Ambassador to South Africa Brent Bozell III, left, poses for a photograph after presenting letters of credence to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, right, at Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria April 8, 2026. (Phill Magakoe/AFP via Getty Images)

The spokesperson added that Trump has demanded South Africa formally designate rural crime as a priority crime and "expand alternatives to the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment ownership requirements, such as equity equivalent investment programs."

Regarding farmers, the State Department spokesperson said South African politicians "threaten to confiscate their farms without compensation and support a corrupt, race-based scoring system that discriminates against Afrikaners and other minorities in employment."

"The lack of a meaningful response to these requests made clear that the South African government does not want a constructive relationship with the United States and is willing to continue pursuing oppressive policies that disadvantage all South Africans," the spokesperson continued.
Nearly 13,000 South African refugees, most of them Afrikaners, have been flown to the U.S. during fiscal year 2026. That number is expected to increase by another 17,500 refugees in fiscal year 2027.

"As directed by President Trump, we are prioritizing the resettlement of Afrikaners in South Africa escaping government-sponsored race-based discrimination," the State Department spokesperson said.
Paul Tilsley is a veteran correspondent who has reported from four continents for more than three decades. Based in Johannesburg, South Africa, he can be followed on X @paultilsley.

title: Judge blocks construction on Trump’s D.C.-area arch after commission’s approval
summary: The Trump administration has said it expects to begin construction immediately, but a judge is considering a plan to temporarily halt the project.
story: A federal judge late Thursday temporarily blocked construction on President Donald Trump’s “Triumphal Arch” shortly after a planning commission led by Trump appointees approved it.

U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan granted a temporary restraining order blocking the administration from “initiating, making, or otherwise effectuating any construction, excavation” or other steps in the arch project for 14 days.

Chutkan’s order came within an hour of the National Capital Planning Commission’s approval of the massive and controversial arch project, which would sit in Memorial Circle between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

The District of Columbia and Virginia, who are suing over the project, filed a motion for the temporary restraining order. In an opinion accompanying her order Chutkan said they have demonstrated a likelihood of standing to sue and an immediate harm.
Chutkan wrote in the opinion that “the harm is certain” and that the Trump administration has said it was ready to start construction almost immediately after the commission’s approval.
The commission passed the motion to approve final site building plans 8-4, with the four votes in opposition coming from commissioners who were not appointed by Trump.
Rep. Don Beyer, D-Va., whose district includes the cemetery, applauded the ruling and accused Trump of trying to bypass legal barriers.

“This fight is not over. While this decision prevents Donald Trump from immediately implementing his plans to create a monument to his own ego, the courts and Congress must put in place permanent safeguards to stop the Trump Administration from violating the law and proceeding with this project,” Beyer said in a statement.
The Department of Interior and National Park Service did not immediately respond to requests for comment about Chutkan’s order early Friday.
The commission gave the project a green light after a hearing at which scores of area residents lined up to voice their opposition to the project.

Public comment at the hearing lasted more than nine hours, which commission Chair Mark Paoletta said was “more than ever.” The comments mostly related to the impact on Arlington National Cemetery, which is the final resting place of the nation’s fallen service members, as well as the project’s height, scale and safety.

Paoletta, who is general counsel at the Office of Management and Budget and was appointed chairman of the commission in August, said at the meeting that it was a “national disgrace” that such a memorial had not already been built. He also praised Trump’s “monumental vision,” saying it would be “the grandest arch ever built by mankind.”

The virtual meeting was interrupted for around 30 minutes during public comments by what Paoletta said was a “malicious attack” that caused the site to crash. He said it’s the “first time this has ever happened.”
Close to 130 members of the public were signed up to speak.
“We’ll have this thing done, whether it’s past midnight or not,” Paoletta said after the interruption. The vote ended in the 10 p.m. hour.
Reps. Brian Mast, R-Fla., and Andrew Clyde, R-Ga., spoke in favor of the project, while Beyer expressed concern over the project and criticized the Trump administration over the approval process.
The governments of Virginia and the District of Columbia have argued the project is illegal.

They asked a judge to immediately halt any construction in a bid to head off possible legal gamesmanship by the administration, citing its earlier destruction of the East Wing of the White House to build a ballroom that includes national security measures.

“It is entirely foreseeable that, once construction begins, Defendants will argue, as they have done in other cases, that an order halting construction would irreparably harm the federal government, pose security risks, and impermissibly alter the status quo they have unilaterally created,” they said. “The Court should not allow this cynical gambit to succeed.”
Following Thursday’s vote, attorneys for the Justice Department filed a document informing Chutkan, the judge, who had asked to be notified after the commission took action.

Trump has said the arch would celebrate the nation’s 250th anniversary and include a military complex with drones and snipers, which he said would be important for national security. The final plans submitted to the commission, however, did not mention drones, ammunition storage or sniper positions.

Asked about the omission at the hearing, Greg Wischer, deputy chief of staff at the Interior Department, said the current “design is capable of hosting national security functions,” but details of those functions aren’t public and have been filed under seal in the court case.
Preservationists and military veterans first sued to block the project this year, arguing that it needed to be authorized by Congress and that the site was improper.

“Its location on Memorial Circle would situate the monument on an axis between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery, obstructing a line of sight that was designed to represent the unification of the Nation following the Civil War and that has existed for nearly a century,” they said.

Testifying at the meeting Thursday, one of the plaintiffs, Vietnam War veteran Michael Lemmon, who was U.S. ambassador to Armenia during the Clinton administration, called the planned arch “frankly blasphemous.”

Virginia and the District of Columbia filed their own action to stop the project last week, contending it “defies at least five federal statutes,” including one that “generally limits buildings in the District to a maximum height of 130 feet.”
The 250-foot arch “would exceed that limit almost twice over.”
They also argued it would harm both D.C. and Virginia residents.

“The Arch is slated to be built on a busy traffic circle that abuts the border between the jurisdictions, at the center of a historic viewshed, in a river whose environment the District has a statutory responsibility to protect,” their suit said.

“Both the construction of the Arch and the completed monument will disrupt the operations of both jurisdictions, impair their ability to carry out their responsibilities under federal and local law, and require the expenditure of substantial resources to mitigate and address those impacts,” they added.

In court filings, the administration countered that the city and state don’t have standing to sue and that Congress gave the project the green light about a century ago, when it “authorized erecting and redesigning 166-foot-tall columns surmounted by statues — exceeding any applicable height limits — and those columns have not yet been built.”
Attorneys for the city and Virginia called those arguments “implausible” and said those columns had initially been planned to be built with the Memorial Bridge before the idea was dropped.
“As Defendants do not dispute, the Memorial Bridge Act nowhere mentions an arch,” they said.
Chutkan in her Thursday opinion did not seem impressed with the administration’s argument about the 1925 act.
“Merely to state this argument is to reveal its flaws,” she wrote.

“The sheer improbability that a 100-year-old statute would contain authority, unknown to every previous administration, to erect a 250-foot arch at a principal location in the Nation’s capital indicates how far Defendants must stretch to justify this project,” Chutkan said in her opinion.

title: Pete Hegseth strikes defiant tone in face of impeachment threat
summary: Many lawmakers, including some Republicans, have criticized the defense secretary over his handling of the Iran war.
story: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday dismissed a renewed effort in the House to bring articles of impeachment against him as early as next week.

In a video on social media, Hegseth said, “A disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democrat allies, has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly, just like they tried against President Trump twice.”

Hegseth was referring to Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., who said Wednesday that he plans to reintroduce articles of impeachment when the House is back in session. Lawmakers are scheduled to return to Washington on Monday.
“It’s all about the politics of personal destruction,” Hegseth added. “Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me. You can rest assured of that.”
In the more-than-five-minute video, Hegseth only briefly touched on the Iran war — a driving force behind the effort to impeach him, as well as GOP losses in this week’s midterm elections.
Massie, who lost his GOP primary after he crossed Trump, urged Trump on Thursday to replace Hegseth while he still has a GOP majority in the Senate.
“My Hegseth impeachment resolution is a much gentler version of what’s coming when Dem’s control Congress. They’ll have hearings & trials,” he said on X.
“There is one contingency in which I won’t reintroduce the articles of impeachment: Hegseth resigns,” Massie wrote Wednesday.
Numerous Democrats have indicated a desire to oust Hegseth since their midterm election wins, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who is poised to be the next speaker.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Trump said Wednesday that he is not planning to replace Hegseth, and he said Thursday that Hegseth “has done a fantastic job” and “probably has opposition” over the actions he has taken, including purging military leadership.

Trump has told some allies he is considering replacing Hegseth, asking them who they think should succeed him, two people familiar with discussions told NBC News this week. He has previously insisted that he was not considering dismissing department heads just days before they were shown the door.
Massie tried to force a vote on impeaching Hegseth in September, but his efforts were stunted when House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., sent the House home early.
He would need several Republicans to join all Democrats in supporting the impeachment measure for it to succeed.

The House has impeached only two Cabinet officials in history — former President Joe Biden’s homeland security secretary, Alejandro Mayorkas, in a partisan vote, and William Belknap, the secretary of war in the 1870s. No Cabinet members have ever been convicted by the Senate.

title: We want to hear your experience with changes to student loan repayment plans
summary: If you’re a student borrower who was required to transition to another plan this year, share your story.
story: President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” has transformed the sprawling federal student loan system — and student borrowers are feeling the effects of the most consequential changes.
For Subscribers

This year, the approximately 7.5 million student borrowers under the Biden-era Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, plan had to select a new one. So far, about 2 million borrowers have done so, after the Education Department warned that the SAVE plan was “illegal” and would be discontinued. The remaining borrowers who did not select a new plan were set to start receiving notices this month informing them that they missed a final deadline and were automatically moved to a new plan.
For Subscribers

The Trump administration has said ending the SAVE plan would help streamline repayment programs while ensuring borrowers are paying off what they owe to the federal government. But student advocacy groups fear lower-income borrowers who had benefited from smaller monthly payments — or even qualified to make no payments at all based on their income — will end up with significantly higher bills under the other available plans.
We want to hear from you, whether you’re in this situation or are facing another challenge related to the recent student loan changes. Please share your experience by filling out the form below.

title: Muscle health is key to longevity. Here’s how to measure yours.
summary: Body mechanics experts say muscle health is linked to our longevity and how well we fight off disease.
story: Muscle health is linked to how well we fight off disease and our longevity. But healthy muscles aren’t just about the size of a bicep or how much we weigh.

An international team of kinesiologists and nutrition experts recently urged doctors to pay more attention to skeletal muscle quality and the ratio of muscle to fat as a key to “metabolic regulation, immune function and overall vitality and functioning.”

“Muscle health estimation could be as important as measuring somebody’s blood pressure,” said longevity expert Dr. Nicolaas Deutz, a professor in the Department of Kinesiology and Sport Management at Texas A&M University and a co-author of the expert review. Kinesiology is the study of physical activity and body mechanics.
Healthy muscles not only help you move safely, they’re also the body’s main storage system for blood sugar, which maintains an active metabolism and lowers inflammation in the body.
Muscle health is usually associated with muscle size in younger people, but that relationship becomes less clear as we get older, said Deutz.
In fact, mass is only a part of overall muscle health. For instance, women generally have lower overall muscle mass than men, yet their muscle health is generally comparable to men’s.

A more complete picture of muscle includes strength, balance, physical function, activity levels and the amount of fat stored within the muscle itself, said Dr. Fatima Cody Stanford, an obesity medicine physician-scientist at Mass General Brigham.
How to prevent muscle loss

There’s growing awareness of how muscle health plays a role in longevity and metabolic diseases such as Type 2 diabetes, especially in the wake of the phenomenal popularity of GLP-1 medications. Drugs such as Ozempic and Zepbound have been shown to improve blood sugar, blood pressure and cardiovascular risk, but they’re also linked to loss of both fat and lean mass, including skeletal muscles.
Stanford, who is also associate professor of medicine and pediatrics at Harvard Medical School, said people taking GLP-1s need adequate nutrition to preserve muscle function.

“As a person loses substantial body weight, the body requires less muscle to carry that weight, and reductions in fat within muscle may improve muscle quality and function,” Stanford said. “At the same time, older adults, individuals with frailty or low baseline muscle mass, and people who are losing weight rapidly warrant particularly close attention to strength, function, protein intake and resistance exercise.”
A sufficient amount of high-quality daily protein — including fish, poultry, eggs, dairy, tofu, beans, lentils, nuts and seeds — helps protect against muscle loss, Stanford said.
The U.S. dietary guidelines encourage people to prioritize protein with nutritious, minimally processed foods at every meal, recommending 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight.
For Subscribers
Staying active — working in the yard, walking or weight training — strengthens different muscle groups, Deutz said.
If lifting heavy gym weights isn’t appealing, resistance exercises can effectively preserve muscle strength and function, particularly during weight loss.
“Body-weight exercises, resistance bands, machines or supervised strength work can all be appropriate depending on the individual’s mobility, fitness level and medical history,” Stanford said.
How to measure muscle health
Muscle power is the ability to produce force quickly, and handgrip strength is one of the simplest ways to measure it.

“An often-overlooked consideration is muscle power — the ability to produce force quickly, which declines earlier and more rapidly with aging than muscle strength,” said Stephen J. Carter, associate professor in the kinesiology department at the School of Public Health — Bloomington Indiana University. “From a practical perspective, muscle power is more relevant to daily life than simply strength.”
Grip strength measures the force generated when squeezing a handheld tool called a dynamometer.
While “low” strength depends on factors like age and BMI, a large analysis of grip strength of over 20,000 older men and women defined it as less than 57 pounds for men and 35 pounds for women.
For Subscribers
Fortunately, targeted resistance training can successfully improve the numbers.

Carter recommended resistance training, such as free weights, weight machines, resistance bands or body-weight exercises like push-ups, two to three times weekly, progressing gradually to a higher intensity to build more muscle.
Other functional tests can help evaluate broader endurance, power and mobility:

The 6-Minute Walk Test: Measures how far a person can walk in six minutes. It’s a gauge of lung and cardiovascular fitness. The Timed Up and Go Test: Assesses fall risk and mobility and can easily be performed at home.The 30-Second Chair Stand Test: Tests lower-body strength by counting the number of times someone gets up from a chair in 30 seconds without using arms.The 5-Repetition Sit-to-Stand Test: Measures lower-body strength and mobility by timing how fast someone can perform five repetitions from sitting to standing position without using arms. It’s a measure of balance, muscle strength and flexibility.

The Timed Up and Go Test: Assesses fall risk and mobility and can easily be performed at home.
The 30-Second Chair Stand Test: Tests lower-body strength by counting the number of times someone gets up from a chair in 30 seconds without using arms.

The 5-Repetition Sit-to-Stand Test: Measures lower-body strength and mobility by timing how fast someone can perform five repetitions from sitting to standing position without using arms. It’s a measure of balance, muscle strength and flexibility.

title: The U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October, a bright spot for the economy
summary: The U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October, a surprisingly strong number that includes what appear to be some AI-related construction and manufacturing jobs.
story: The U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, a surprisingly strong number that includes what appear to be some AI-related construction and manufacturing jobs.

American workers have so far seen relatively few benefits from the artificial intelligence boom that has driven the stock market higher and fueled trillions of dollars in spending by the world’s top tech giants.
The unemployment rate in October dropped to 4.1%, extending a near-historic low streak.
The report “added to evidence of labor-market stability” and consumer resilience, said Jennifer Timmerman, senior investment strategy analyst at Wells Fargo.
While that steady figure reflects fulsome employment across the nation, economists also say that it reflects a kind of stagnation.
“The problem is the low rate of turnover,” said Diane Swonk, chief economist at KPMG. “Fewer people are entering the labor force.”
Sluggish wage growth did not meaningfully improve last month, however. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year ago, which continues to track well below the rate of inflation.

Inflation is 3.7% and on the upswing, as of the most recent consumer price index released Oct. 14. Business inflation is rising even faster, a likely sign of what’s to come for consumers at grocery stores and retail outlets.
Friday’s report also showed strong upward revisions to recent jobs data.

Net job gains for August were revised up by 53,000, from 133,000 to 186,000. September was revised up by 31,000, from 29,000 positions added to 60,000, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said in a statement.
The report was “a blowout,” said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. But she cautioned that any impact from the additional jobs would be blunted by other economic headwinds.
It “doesn’t erase this painful fact: Inflation has wiped out all wage gains for 7 straight months,” Long wrote  on X.
“In fact, the inflation resurgence has been so strong that it’s basically wiped out all wage gains since January 2025.”
For Subscribers
Friday’s jobs report also suggests the sprawling AI data center buildout across the country could be supporting at least some construction and manufacturing jobs.
For Subscribers
Manufacturing roles in October rose by 19,000 last month, according to BLS data. The sector has added more than 100,000 jobs total since its recent low, in December 2025.
The agency noted that within the manufacturing sector, the subsets of computer and electronics manufacturing, machinery manufacturing and what it called “primary metal manufacturing” led the gains.
Nonresidential construction jobs also jumped by almost 3,000 roles in October, likely an indication of demand for data center jobs.

In contrast to the commercial construction industry, the home building and contracting sector shed more than 15,000 jobs last month. High interest rates have paralyzed the residential real estate market and cut demand for the kind of refinancing loans that typically fund home renovations.

Other sectors that have been largely powering U.S. job growth for years also showed strong gains in the month. The healthcare sector added 42,000 jobs, which the BLS said was higher than its average monthly gain over the past year.
The professional and business services sector, as the agency classifies it, gained 70,000 jobs, blowing past its average monthly gain of 15,000 over the past year.
Retailers also appear to have started strong holiday hiring, with firms classified as “general merchandise retailers” adding more than 18,000 roles.
Friday’s data also bolstered the case for an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve when it meets Dec. 8 and 9.
Following the BLS release, the odds of a December interest rate hike jumped to nearly 80%.

title: LeBron James took a risk going to the 76ers this offseason. So far, it’s paying off.
summary: James, who switched teams for the fourth time in free agency over the summer, has helped lead the Philadelphia 76ers to the hottest start in the NBA.
story: When his agent, Rich Paul, revealed on a whiteboard the teams likeliest to sign him in the summer, LeBron James appeared to be choosing among five contenders after he entered free agency: the Philadelphia 76ers, the Miami Heat, the Minnesota Timberwolves, the Denver Nuggets and the Cleveland Cavaliers.
James, in something of a surprise, picked the 76ers. And through the (very) early part of this season, he appears to have chosen wisely.

Philadelphia is 8-1 after a win over the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday night. The 76ers have the most wins in the NBA entering Friday, and their high-powered starting five has jelled quickly to form an undeniable title contender.
The starting five
In addition to signing James, Philly traded for swingman Jaylen Brown in the offseason, forming a starting five of James, Brown, Tyrese Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe and Joel Embiid.
Those five players have combined for 36 All-Star selections, five MVP awards and five Finals MVP awards. So it’s perhaps unsurprising the group has been great together on the floor.

In 77 minutes together across five games, the Sixers’ starting five has outscored opponents by 15 points. Philadelphia’s opening quintet is dominating defensively, holding opponents to only 95.4 points per 100 possessions. (For context, the league’s best defense entering Thursday was holding opponents to 103 points per 100 possessions.)

“Our defense is going to be our identity,” James said Wednesday after the win over the Pistons. “We have a lot of scoring. We know that from individuals. We’re still figuring out that side of the floor out on the offensive side. Defensively, that’s where we are going to make our mark.”

James has meshed well with all of his co-stars so far. All two-man lineups featuring a combo of James plus one of Maxey, Brown, Embiid and Edgecombe have outscored opponents through the team’s first nine games.

title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.
story: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday morning after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown against future gains following broad Democratic victories in the midterms.
The tech-focused Nasdaq 100 opened 1.6% higher after plunging 6.3% Thursday, its worst single-day performance since the Covid-19 pandemic as $2.3 billion in market value were erased.
The broader S&P 500 was 0.3% higher after tanking 4.4% Thursday, wiping out $2.8 trillion in paper wealth.

Investors continue to digest the results of Tuesday’s midterms that swept a crop of anti-AI and data center opponent politicians into office, including Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa in Texas, among the largest data center markets in the country. The AI boom has comprised an ever-increasing share of stock gains and economic growth writ-large, making markets increasingly susceptible to any threat to the narrative.

“Markets are being punished according to their dependence on the U.S. AI infrastructure cycle,” Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Singapore-based SAXO Markets, told NBC News in emailed comments.

The newly Democrat-controlled Congress could also tighten scrutiny of the industry, including AI infrastructure projects, which could cause delays and additional costs, adding to worries investors have about the profitability of these investments.

Some analysts viewed Thursday’s dramatic sell-off as overblown —  or at least, merely a sign of some froth coming off an overstretched market rather than the end of the line for the AI investment wave.

In a note to clients Friday, economist and longtime market watcher Ed Yardeni called recent declines “just speed bumps” that may be helping prevent the AI bubble from over-inflating, and that buying opportunities may already be preventing themselves.
Still, he acknowledged risks remain, namely the extent to which AI data centers get delayed or canceled outright.
Volatility is likely to continue until it becomes clearer how much data center construction is truly threatened by newly elected lawmakers.

“This is a stock market that is trying to figure out the right valuations for the AI trade, which is grappling with a swift sentiment shift after the midterm elections,” Alex Guiliano, chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Resonate Wealth Partners, said in a statement.

The Fellow Aiden makes it effortless. It automatically sets the ideal temperature and ratio for light, medium or dark roasts, and it even does cold brew. Brew a single cup or a full pot into the thermal carafe, which keeps coffee warm long after the first toddler interruption.
Season to Taste: Comforting Recipes You Won't Find in a Restaurant

Before kids, I loved to cook. These days, most of my kitchen time goes to buttered noodles, scrambled eggs and sliced berries for my picky eaters. During my nightly scrollfest, I discovered Corre Larkin on Instagram and fell for how simple yet refined her recipes are — it is food even a tired mom can pull off. Her debut cookbook, Season to Taste, has nearly 100 recipes, including Spaghetti with Four Tomatoes to Flavor Bomb Roast Chicken, plus a whole chapter on potatoes. I’m treating myself to this book for Christmas and I know other moms who miss cooking real food would appreciate it, too.
Demarson Tina Hoops

Everyday jewelry can be tricky for moms. Wear anything that dangles too low and you risk it getting ripped off by sticky little hands. These two-tone hoops are fun and geometric but only about an inch long — so they make a statement but are small enough to avoid being grasped and look totally appropriate for school drop-off, the office or dinner out. The two-tone finish goes with both gold and silver jewelry, which makes getting dressed one less decision and the surgical steel posts are made for sensitive ears, so they’re easy to wear all day.

NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans loves her pair, she says she’s worn the earrings to weddings, work and date nights. “I like to mix metals so these are perfect because they sort of bridge the gap between my gold nose ring and permanent bracelets and my diamond and white gold wedding band,” she says. “They never feel heavy either, which I find happens with some fine jewelry.”
Best beauty and wellness gifts for moms
Biodance Real Deep Mask Gift Set

Biodance face masks are popular among NBC Selected editors, and this set lets a busy mom sample four of its most popular formulas. Each one targets a different concern, from hydration and calming to pores and dark spots, with ingredients like collagen, ceramides and niacinamide. Better yet, there’s no need to rinse: She can leave one on overnight and let it work while she sleeps. It’s the ultimate low-effort pampering.
YISE Beauty The Overachiever Brightening & Depuffing Eye Patches

For tired moms, these cooling vitamin C eye patches with peptides and hyaluronic acid can help with dark circles and dryness. “They actually reduce puffiness under my eyes when I wake up and I look brighter and more awake after wearing them for 15 minutes,” says NBC Selected updates editor Mili Godio. “They’re also sticky, which means they aren’t slipping and sliding on my face as I wear them.”
Dr. Dennis Gross DRx Spectralite Faceware Pro LED Mask

This LED mask can turn three minutes into a real self-care moment. That’s the shortest treatment time of any mask we recommend. It uses red light to target fine lines and blue light to fight acne, and she can use one color or both in each session. NBC Selected associate SEO reporter Ashley Morris tested it after the brand sent her a sample. She still uses it a few times a week, usually right after her morning shower. “When I use the mask consistently, my skin has a smoother texture and overall clearer complexion,” she says. It has also helped her with mild breakouts and the occasional flare-up.

title: I asked teens what gifts they actually want — here’s what they said
summary: Looking for gifts for teenage girls and boys? Discover our picks for stylish, practical and personalized presents, with recommendations from real teens.
story: Shopping for teenagers can be tricky. Trends come and go, interests change seemingly overnight and what was considered cool a few months ago might already be out of style. And while teenagers are often pretty vocal about what they like (and especially what they don’t like), finding a gift they’ll actually use and appreciate long term can still feel like a guessing game.

Luckily, I have a few teenagers in my corner. As the oldest of three siblings, including a 16-year-old girl, and as an occasional tutor for high schoolers, I’ve had a front-row seat to the changing trends of today’s teens. I am very good at giving gifts, according to everyone I know. Every year, I arrange dozens of gifts for my large family across many age groups and they all ask me, “how do you do it?” Shopping and testing products for a living helps, but I truly take pride in giving people gifts that make them feel special, and won’t just get added to piles of clutter somewhere. Whether you’re shopping for a fashion-obsessed 13-year-old, a high school athlete or a soon-to-be college student, these are some of the best gifts for teens to consider this year.
The best gifts for teens in 2026

With trends coming and going faster than ever, teens are constantly being told what they should want next. As a big sister, I want my siblings to discover their own taste and understand that the best things aren’t always the trendiest. These gifts strike that balance, with picks that feel exciting now but are useful and special enough to enjoy long after the hype fades.

Best clothing gifts for teens
Lululemon Define Jacket

My 16-year-old sister owns this jacket in three colors and hopes to collect more like they’re Infinity Stones. It’s one of her favorite pieces to wear to school, sports practice and just about everywhere else. Made from Lululemon’s soft, stretchy, sweat-wicking fabric, the Define Jacket has a fitted silhouette, zippered pockets and thumbholes with fold-over cuffs to help keep hands warm. For teens who prefer something roomier, my sister also recommends the brand’s Scuba Evolve Hoodie, which is great for lounging, running errands or layering over workout clothes.
Etam Boat Neck Thermal T-Shirt with Cashmere

Growing up, my mother would make us wear the thickest long johns underneath our school uniforms during the winter. Between the sweating, chafing and bulkiness, I dreaded putting them on. Thankfully, thermal wear has come a long way. I own this cashmere-blend top from Etam in black and blue, and it’s become a cold-weather essential for me. It’s lightweight enough to wear underneath sweaters and jackets without adding bulk, but stylish enough to wear on its own. Think of it as an elevated alternative to traditional thermals.
Duer Tech Fleece Denim Utility Pant

I hate layering leggings or thermals underneath my jeans when it’s cold outside, which is why I’ve become such a fan of Duer’s fleece-lined denim. The brand’s Tech Fleece fabric combines the look of denim with the comfort and warmth of an insulating layer, keeping me cozy without needing to double up on pants. I own a pair and have found them particularly useful during colder months. NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin recommends Duer’s high-rise straight-leg jeans if the teen you’re shopping for prefers a classic denim silhouette.
We can help you find
UGG Women's Classic Ultra Mini Boot

Ugg’s Classic Ultra Mini boots are a great gift for teens who love cozy footwear. Their low-cut silhouette makes them easy to slip on and style with leggings, jeans or sweatpants, while the sheepskin lining adds warmth. They’re especially useful for casual outings, long travel days, quick errands and lounging between activities.
Adidas Samba OG Shoes

For the teen who’s always keeping up with sneaker trends, Adidas’ Samba OG is an option they can always wear. Originally designed as an indoor soccer shoe, the low-profile sneaker has become a casual wardrobe staple that pairs easily with jeans, skirts and wide-leg trousers. If the recipient already owns a pair, consider another Adidas style like the Barreda Lo, Japan or Gazelle Indoor shoes.
Crocs Classic Clog
Every teen has a pair of Crocs and their special collection of Jibbitz. My sister and I have multiples and we welcome new ones every year with gratitude. They’re just so practical.
Best winter jacket gifts for teens
Aritzia The Super Puff Shorty Jacket

Aritzia’s Super Puff is a splurge, but its serious warmth and stylish, oversized look make it a teen gift worth considering. Toronto native and NBC Selected associate reporter Ashley Morris says, “I’ve never had a coat this warm before,” noting she can brave freezing temperatures with just a t-shirt underneath. With multiple lengths, colors and finishes, plus deep pockets for their phone, keys and lip gloss, it’s as practical as it is cool-looking.
The North Face Retro 1996 Nuptse Jacket

The North Face is a reliable option for winter outerwear, and I own a jacket from the brand. The 1996 Retro Nuptse is one of its most recognizable styles, with a boxy silhouette, oversized quilted sections and 700-fill recycled down insulation for warmth. It also has a water-repellent finish and a stowable hood. For teens who want a jacket they can wear to school, on weekend outings and during cold-weather activities, it’s an option that will pair well with most things in their wardrobe.
Hollister Peyton Reversible Puffer Jacket

My 16-year-old sister bought this jacket from Hollister for herself, and it’s become one of her favorite winter purchases. I can see why: The reversible design gives her two different looks in one, with a classic quilted puffer on one side and cozy faux fur on the other. It also has a hood with removable faux fur trim, lined pockets and thumbholes at the cuffs. It’s an especially good gift for fashion-conscious teens who enjoy switching up their style without having to own multiple winter coats.
Best bags and accessory gifts for teens
Nike Varsity Elite Backpack

When I asked my 16-year-old sister what teenagers actually wanted for Christmas, this backpack was the first thing she mentioned. As a student athlete, it was at the very top of her wish list. It has a spacious main compartment that can accommodate a full-size basketball, plus a separate bottom compartment for shoes or sweaty clothes. It’s a practical option for teens balancing school, sports and extracurricular activities, especially those who need something roomy enough to carry their gear throughout the day.
Coach Plaza Bag

In my opinion, Coach has had one of the best brand revivals in recent years, and my sister agrees. She sends links to Coach handbags, shoes and accessories to our family group chat practically every week. For teens interested in starting a handbag collection, I recommend the Coach Plaza Bag. Its simple, streamlined design makes it easy to dress up or down, while its compact size is convenient for carrying everyday essentials. Another option I love is the Coach Brooklyn Shoulder Bag 28, which has a more relaxed silhouette and offers more space inside.
Coach Utility Tote

For teens who prefer a structured, functional bag, the Coach Utility Tote is worth considering. Made with canvas, leather and other durable materials, it has a spacious interior that can accommodate a laptop up to 16 inches, along with books, documents and other everyday essentials. The interior snap pocket provides extra organization, while the graphic design adds personality to it. I also recommend the Coach Harrison Pouch for someone who prefers carrying fewer belongings.
Longchamp Le Pliage Original L Tote

Practically every woman in my family owns a Longchamp Le Pliage tote, and for good reason. Its lightweight, foldable design makes it incredibly convenient, whether you’re carrying school supplies, work essentials, a change of clothes or items for an overnight trip. It’s one of those bags that can remain useful long after the teenage years. For teens who prefer keeping their hands free, I also recommend the Longchamp Le Pliage Original M Backpack.
New Balance Urban Backpack

My sister uses the New Balance Urban Backpack, and it’s a great under-$100 gift for teens who need to carry a little bit of everything. The unisex design has dedicated storage for a laptop, phone and water bottles, plus plenty of room for a change of shoes. Its durable nylon construction makes it a practical pick for school, sports and travel.
Adidas Defender Duffel Bag

The Adidas Defender Duffel Bag is a practical gift for student athletes and teens who are constantly on the go. Its roomy design provides space for workout clothes, sneakers, sports equipment and everyday essentials, making it useful for everything from after school practices to weekend trips. It’s also a more affordable alternative to some premium sports and travel bags.
BaubleBar Fine Line Custom iPhone Case

I once spotted someone in my office carrying this phone case and immediately stopped her to ask where it was from. I liked it so much that I attended a BaubleBar event to see more of the brand’s personalized accessories and couldn’t wait to get one of my own. The Fine Line Custom iPhone Case can be personalized with a name, making it a fun way for teens to express their style through something they use every day. It’s a particularly good gift if you want something thoughtful without having to guess their clothing or shoe size.
BaubleBar The Ultimate Custom Bead Kit

Nowadays, even backpacks and handbags seem to need their own accessories, and this customizable bead kit lets teens create charms that reflect their personal style. It has supplies for making up to six bag charms, including colorful beads, alphabet letters, decorative motifs and paracord bases with carabiner clasps. Teens can spell out names, initials and inside jokes, or mix different designs to match their bags. It’s a fun activity for creative teens to enjoy alone or with friends, and I also recommend checking out BaubleBar’s ready-made bag charms.
Weatherman Travel Umbrella

An umbrella might not sound like the most exciting gift, but I own Weatherman’s Travel Umbrella and genuinely can’t recommend it enough. It’s stylish, compact and convenient to carry around, especially if you live in a place where the weather changes throughout the day. Instead of repeatedly replacing flimsy umbrellas that break during storms, I think investing in a high-quality one is worth it. It’s an especially practical gift for teens who commute to school on the train or bus.
Gemi Hand Santizer + Serum with Key Ring

Hand sanitizer is something most teens already carry, so why not make it feel like a cute accessory? We’ve been testing Gemi’s Hand Sanitizer + Serum in the office, and I’ve already received compliments on the scent. The bottle has a sleek, capless design that opens and locks with a simple twist, while the attached key ring makes it easy to put on a backpack, purse or set of keys. It’s a small, practical gift that feels more thoughtful than your average bottle of sanitizer, and if you get your teen a bedazzling kit, they can bling it out however they like.
Best jewelry gifts for teens
Made By Mary Birthstone Stacking Ring

Personalized jewelry is one of my favorite things to give because it feels thoughtful without necessarily requiring an extravagant budget. I own this birthstone stacking ring from Made by Mary, and it’s such a beautiful, meaningful piece. Each ring features a stone representing a birth month, making it a great option for teens who are starting to build their jewelry collection. Its delicate design also makes it easy to stack with other rings.
Demarson Eva Pavé Pink Ear Cuff

My sister is constantly begging our parents for more ear piercings, but since they have yet to give in, I’ve been encouraging her to experiment with ear cuffs instead. I’ve tried plenty myself, and Demarson’s are among the most comfortable I’ve worn. This pink pavé cuff adds a fun pop of color without requiring an additional piercing, and it’s so lightweight that I sometimes forget I’m wearing it. I’ve even fallen asleep with one on. It’s a great gift for teens who want to experiment with their jewelry without committing to another piercing.
The best beauty and self-care gifts for teens
Shark Silki Straight Wet to Dry Straightener + Blow Dryer

Wash days can take hours, especially if you have thick, curly or coily hair. My 16-year-old sister and I both have type 4 natural hair, and Shark’s SilkiPro has made our wash days significantly easier and faster. We use it constantly because it combines drying and straightening in one tool, so we don’t have to switch between multiple devices. It also comes with interchangeable comb attachments to help detangle, stretch and smooth hair. While we particularly appreciate how well it works on our natural hair, it’s designed for different hair types, making it a versatile gift for teens who enjoy styling their hair.
Dazzle Dry Build Your System Kit

For teens who love getting their nails done, Dazzle Dry’s Build Your System Kit makes it easier to experiment with manicures at home. The system includes nail prep, base coat, lacquer, top coat and a Revive solution to help maintain the products. Unlike gel manicures, it doesn’t require a UV or LED lamp, and the brand says nails dry completely in five minutes after applying the top coat. It also comes off with regular nail polish remover, making it a convenient alternative to acrylics and gel manicures.

My sister and I are currently testing the kit, and I think it’s an especially fun option for teens who want their nails done but whose parents don’t want paying ever-increasing salon prices. The average manicure lasts me about two to three weeks.
Saie The Vanity Case

If the teen you’re shopping for is anything like my sister, they’re probably spending a good portion of their allowance on makeup and skin care without having much of an organizational system in place. That’s where Saie’s Vanity Case comes in handy. The structured case has a carrying handle, zippered closure and removable interior organizer to keep beauty products from getting lost or scattered across a bathroom counter.

NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio has this case, and she loves that it keeps her makeup and tools orderly so they don’t get mixed up and hard to find during travel. It’s a useful gift for teens building their makeup collection, and it’s convenient for sleepovers, trips and getting ready in the car or on the train. You can also get a mini version of the case.
Best tech gifts for teens
Lofree Flow Lite 84 Keys Mechanical Keyboard

Whether they use their setup for gaming, tutoring or homework, this low-profile mechanical keyboard can make time at their desk more enjoyable. The keys have a satisfying “creamy” sound without being too loud, and I find them easy to type on, especially since my hands are prone to finger fatigue. Bluetooth is also simple to set up, and the compact 84-key layout won’t overwhelm their desk.
Kodak Printomatic + Instant Print Digital Camera

Kodak’s Printomatic+ Instant Print Digital Camera combines the fun of digital photography with the nostalgia of physical prints. It lets users snap photos and print them on ink-free, sticky-backed paper, which is perfect for decorating journals, lockers, scrapbooks and bedroom walls. My sister and I have been testing the camera and have really enjoyed using it so far. It’s a fun way to make memories feel a little more tangible instead of leaving all your favorite photos buried in your camera roll.
Kodak Step Instant Smartphone Photo Printer

If the teen you’re shopping for already takes plenty of photos on their phone, the Kodak Step Instant Smartphone Photo Printer is another great gift option. The compact printer connects to a smartphone via Bluetooth and produces 2-by-3-inch prints using Kodak’s ink-free technology. The prints have adhesive backs, so teens can use them to decorate photo albums, journals and other personal belongings. My sister and I have also been testing this printer and have liked it so far. I particularly recommend it for teens who love scrapbooking, journaling or decorating their spaces with photos.
Sony Stranger Things USB-C Wired Headphones (Pre-order)

“Stranger Things” has introduced a new generation to ’80s style, and these limited-edition Sony headphones lean all the way into the nostalgia. Inspired by Max’s signature headphones and the Upside Down, they have interchangeable earpads in different colors and an engraved “Stranger Things” logo. They’re wired with USB-C, so teens can plug them directly into compatible phones, tablets and laptops without worrying about charging or Bluetooth pairing. And while they nod to the Walkman headphones of the past, the sound has been enhanced to meet the listening quality of today, according to Sony. The $79.99 headphones are available for pre-order now.
JBL PartyBox 330 Portable Party Speaker Bundle with Microphones

For teens who love music, singing or hosting friends, I can’t recommend a JBL PartyBox speaker and EasySing microphones enough. I go to karaoke almost every week, but paying for karaoke rooms in New York City gets expensive. Having this setup at home lets me sing with my friends whenever I want without the extra expense.

The PartyBox I’ve used has wheels and a handle for easy transportation, while its powerful sound and built-in light show make any room feel like a party. The microphones make you feel like you’re performing in a stadium, and I love that I can set the volume for use in my apartment without overwhelming my neighbors. It’s a gift I wish I’d had in college, and one that’s just as fun for teens as it is for the whole family.
Beats Studio Pro Headphones

I own the Beats Studio Pro headphones, and I love how stylish and versatile they are. They offer active noise cancellation and wireless connectivity, and they’re compatible with both Apple and Android devices, so they’re a great option regardless of which phone the recipient uses. They’re particularly useful for teens who want to block out distractions while studying or listen to their favorite playlists on the go.
OpenAI ChatGPT Gift Card

According to my brother and his friends, AI tools are becoming an increasingly useful part of how they study, especially for subjects involving data, coding and complex concepts. For older teens who enjoy learning new skills, an OpenAI gift card can help cover eligible ChatGPT subscriptions and features. It can be a useful gift for students who want help practicing concepts, organizing study materials or working through programming problems. For teens who prefer a more structured study tool, I also recommend considering a Quizlet gift card.
Best cozy gifts and bedroom accessory gifts for teens
Lola Blanket Original

I’ve tried plenty of blankets, but my Lola Blanket is genuinely one of the best I’ve ever owned. It’s incredibly soft, comes in beautiful, rich colors and has become a staple of my nighttime routine. Although Lola Blankets have become popular, I think their appeal goes beyond the trend. Mine feels luxurious, and I reach for it constantly, whether I’m watching a movie, reading or winding down for bed. The blankets are definitely a splurge, so I’d recommend looking out for a sale. For teens who love cozying up at home, it’s a gift they’re likely to use every day.
P.J. Salvage 3-Piece Flannel PJ Set

You can never go wrong with a cozy pair of pajamas, especially during the colder months. Our team tested popular pajamas from P.J. Salvage last year, and we absolutely loved them. This three-piece flannel set is a great gift for teens who enjoy spending their evenings lounging, watching movies or having sleepovers with friends. It includes a long-sleeve shirt, matching drawstring pants and a matching hair wrap.
Owala FreeSip Holiday Collection

title: A college student was held at knifepoint by his brother. He escaped, and police shot him.
summary: Maverick Lyon, a college lacrosse player, filed a federal civil rights case alleging excessive force and negligence on the part of the city of Albany and Benton County.
story: A college athlete in Oregon who was shot multiple times by police while he was escaping a dangerous encounter with his brother alleges excessive force and negligence in a federal civil rights case filed Wednesday.

Maverick Lyon, a college lacrosse player, was home in Albany on Jan. 6 when his brother, who had relapsed into drug use, held him at knifepoint, attorneys with Stritmatter Law said in the suit. Their father called Albany police after he saw the altercation on a security video in the family’s home.
Lyon grabbed another knife in self-defense during the encounter and managed to escape through the back door, the lawsuit says.

According to the suit, after Lyon dropped the knife, police shot him at least five times. His injuries led to four weeks in the hospital and serious operations. The lawsuit says Lyon was shot even though he followed police commands.

Benton County said in response to an NBC News request that it does not comment on pending litigation. The city of Albany, which is also named as a defendant, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Lyon’s attorneys said in a statement that after the shooting, surgeons “removed half of his right lung, his spleen, his appendix, and performed extensive reconstructive surgery on his digestive system.”

His parents, David and Laura Lyon, said in a statement: “I have always believed that when you call 911, help is coming. I never imagined that making that call would leave me wondering if my son was going to survive.”

“Our family has been through something no family should ever have to experience. I called the police that day because I wanted to protect Maverick, and instead, the very people I called for help ended up nearly taking his life,” they said.

According to the lawsuit, the family’s ordeal began after Jan. 5, when David and Laura Lyon told a Benton County probation officer that their elder son, Dakota, was “acting dangerously toward family members” and had relapsed into using drugs. They asked the county to take Dakota Lyon into custody, but it declined to, according to the lawsuit.
“The next day, David called 911 after Dakota’s drug-induced behavior escalated to taking their youngest son, Maverick Lyon, hostage at knifepoint inside the home,” the lawsuit says.

Albany police surrounded the Lyon house, where officers could identify Maverick and Dakota through a window, according to the lawsuit. Maverick was mouthing “help me” to the officers through the window, it says. It also alleges that police were familiar with Dakota Lyon and knew Maverick was the victim in the incident.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Police told Maverick to come outside and drop a knife he had grabbed in self-defense, but “when Maverick did as instructed, Albany Police officers shot Maverick at least five times in the chest, back, and face after he had dropped the knife, came outside, and presented no threat,” the lawsuit says.
It says that rather than provide Maverick with medical assistance, police “yelled at Maverick to roll over and submit to handcuffing while Maverick was on the ground bleeding.”
The Albany Police Department said in a statement at the time that its officers were involved in a shooting after they responded to a domestic disturbance and encountered a person with a knife.
Two officers fired their weapons, striking the person who had the knife, it said, adding that the officers “immediately rendered medical aid until emergency personnel arrived.”

Dakota Lyon was later sentenced to more than six years for the incident with his brother. According to KVAL-TV of Eugene, he acknowledged his responsibility in the case, and his attorney said Lyon wished he could have taken the bullets instead of his brother.
The lawsuit alleges excessive force, battery, negligence and violation of Maverick Lyon’s Fourth Amendment rights. It seeks a jury trial and damages.
Benton County District Attorney Ryan S. Joslin previously ruled that the shooting was justified.

Joslin said that after an investigation, he determined that the officers’ decision to “fire their duty weapons in this case was based on an objectively reasonable belief that to do so was necessary in order to protect their own lives or the lives of fellow officers.”

The decision “must be made in light of what the officers knew and perceived leading up to and at the exact time their decision was made,” he said. “In this case, the officers, in real time, had only fractions of a second to decide how to act.”
The district attorney’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
David and Laura Lyon said they support their son’s lawsuit.

“We cannot change what happened that day, but we want answers, accountability, and changes that help prevent another family from experiencing the pain ours has,” they said in their statement. “Most importantly, we want Maverick to have every opportunity to heal, move forward, and live the life he deserves.”

title: Justice Department moves to toss Steve Bannon’s conviction tied to Congress’ Jan. 6 investigation
summary: The administration “harbors significant doubts” about the trial’s fairness, a top official said in a court filing.
story: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration moved Thursday to vacate the conviction of Steve Bannon on two counts of contempt of Congress in connection with its investigation into the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol.
Bannon, a White House chief strategist and senior counselor during President Donald Trump’s first term, served a four-month prison sentence after the conviction in 2022.

The Justice Department wrote in a court filing Thursday that it had determined “dismissal is in the interests of justice because, in an exercise of its prosecutorial discretion, the Executive Branch does not believe that it is appropriate to pursue contempt of Congress charges against a former advisor to the President who did not comply with a subpoena investigating the events of January 6, 2021, based on an asserted belief that he was protected by executive privilege.”
The administration “harbors significant doubts” about the trial’s fairness, it said in the motion, which was signed by Deputy Associate Attorney General Michael Weisbuch.

“President Trump has expressed grave concerns about the Biden Administration’s prosecutions related to the events of January 6, 2021, granting a large number of pardons and commutations,” the motion said.
The Justice Department filing added that in light of Trump’s actions, seeking to affirm Bannon’s conviction “is inconsistent with this Administration’s enforcement priorities.”
Bannon’s legal team did not oppose the motion.
For Subscribers
U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols previously denied a motion to dismiss the indictment, saying in August that the government had not adequately described why it wanted to do so.
For Subscribers
The Supreme Court had sent the case back to Nichols, wiping out an appeals court ruling that upheld the jury’s verdict.
Acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter previously served as Bannon’s counsel. His name does not appear on the Justice Department’s court filing.
Trump pardoned hundreds of Jan. 6 defendants on his first day back in office.

title: Head of DOJ Civil Rights Division resigns after GOP midterms loss
summary: Harmeet Dhillon oversaw a massive overhaul of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, targeting universities and focusing on culture war issues.
story: WASHINGTON — Harmeet Dhillon, the Republican attorney who oversaw a massive overhaul of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, submitted her resignation Thursday.

Attorney General Todd Blanche posted on X that he has accepted Dhillon’s resignation. He wrote that she “defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor” and that the DOJ “is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors.”
Dhillon posted Thursday on X that the job had been the “honor of a lifetime.”
“We ushered in the downfall of illegal DEI, we fought to protect women and girls’ sports, and so much more,” she wrote.

The departure of Dhillon, who had a long history of working as an election lawyer for the GOP, comes just two days after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the midterm elections.

Under Dhillon’s leadership, the Civil Rights Division led some of the Trump administration’s most controversial legal maneuvers, including lawsuits that cited claims of discrimination at elite universities. The division declined to open a use-of-force investigation into the ICE officer who shot and killed Renee Nicole Good in Minnesota earlier this year.

Her office also filed lawsuits against 30 states and Washington, D.C., in an effort to obtain voter registration lists from the states in the months before the election, with federal judges dismissing 27 of those cases. Dhillon was a regular presence on conservative media in the run-up to Tuesday’s elections, promoting the work of the Civil Rights Division.
Dhillon is set to speak at the Donald Trump Ballroom at the Mar-a-Lago Club during the Conservative Political Action Committee’s Circle Retreat and Gala on Thursday.
Bloomberg Law first reported her resignation plans.

Dhillon’s office recently attempted to indict Cassidy Hutchinson, the former Trump administration official who testified before the House Jan. 6 committee about Trump’s actions during the Capitol siege.

Her office also brought a criminal case against former CNN journalist Don Lemon and protesters over a demonstration at a church in Minnesota under a statute historically used to protect reproductive rights facilities.

Stacey Young, the executive director of the group Justice Connection, called Dhillon “the most destructive, lawless, and hateful head of the Civil Rights Division in DOJ history,” and said in a statement that she “wielded the enormous power of the Justice Department to threaten universities, state and local officials, and election workers in spurious cases that rarely won in court.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Dhillon “decimated” the Civil Rights Division, Young said, and called on the incoming Senate “to exercise its full advice and consent powers to ensure the next Assistant Attorney General fulfills the division’s congressional mandate to enforce all Americans’ civil rights diligently and fairly.”

Kristen Clarke, the NAACP’s general counsel and the former chief of the Civil Rights Division during the Biden administration, said Dhillon “abdicated her responsibility to enforce our nation’s federal civil rights laws and destroyed the crown jewel of the Justice Department.”

Clarke said in a statement that Dhillon “abandoned cases, purged the work force and weaponized the Division to target institutions to achieve illegitimate, partisan goals” and that the NAACP would demand that her replacement “respect the agency’s sacred mission, enforce the law fairly, and protect our civil rights.”

title: Rep. Ro Khanna allies launch a draft campaign for the 2028 presidential race
summary: Exclusive: The California congressman has been traveling the country and building prominence among progressives.
story: Allies of Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., are launching an effort to lay groundwork for him to run for president, the leaders of a new draft committee told NBC News.

Former Rep. Jamaal Bowman, D-N.Y., and progressive strategist Nomiki Konst are co-chairs of the group — “Run Ro” — which can raise money from donors and begin building support for a Khanna candidacy while he continues to weigh a 2028 bid.

The move comes in the immediate aftermath of a midterm election in which voters swept Democrats into power in the House and the Senate, with some high-profile progressives among the big winners. It also comes as the party’s left wing looks for a new champion who can run in the progressive lane that Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., occupied in the 2016 and 2020 presidential nominating contests.
“By launching now, we are trying to ensure that the presidential primary debate is framed from a progressive populist perspective,” Konst said.
The challenges facing a possible Khanna candidacy are immense. Only one person was ever elected to the presidency directly from the House: James Garfield, R-Ohio, in 1880.

Khanna, a fifth-term lawmaker, has made headlines with bipartisan efforts to force the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files and to end the war in Iran. He is nonetheless not even the most famous House progressive considering a presidential bid.
That unofficial title belongs to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., who hasn’t yet said whether she will seek the presidency, run for a Senate seat in New York or remain in the House.

“She is my sister, and I love her,” Bowman said of Ocasio-Cortez, with whom he shared a close alliance in the House. “Ro Khanna has shown the work ethic, the humility and the vision that we need in this moment.”

Khanna, who was a co-chair of Sanders’ 2020 campaign, is also a favorite of progressives around the country. And he has been traveling to early primary states for months. He makes no effort to hide his presidential ambitions, and many of his colleagues believe he will jump into the race.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
He welcomed the draft committee in a statement to NBC News.

“I’m honored that people are encouraging me to run on a platform of Medicare for All, ending foreign wars and taxing the billionaires,” he said. “We need America’s Next New Deal. Whether I run or support someone else is something I will decide with my family after the holidays.”
Asked about a potential presidential bid during an appearance Thursday night on MS NOW, Khanna said, “Yes, I’m thinking about it.”
Konst said the draft committee will allow her and Bowman to organize now so Khanna isn’t late to the game if he does run.

“The centrists organize and strategize early,” she said. “They have their donors, corporate consultants and leaders lined up for years. Building off the lessons of past primaries, our goal is to channel the progressive energy into a vessel for organizing and spreading our winning message early, as we can’t wait for the politics to line up.”
No candidate has yet entered the field for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination.

title: LeBron James took a risk going to the 76ers this offseason. So far, it’s paying off.
summary: James, who switched teams for the fourth time in free agency over the summer, has helped lead the Philadelphia 76ers to the hottest start in the NBA.
story: When his agent, Rich Paul, revealed on a whiteboard the teams likeliest to sign him in the summer, LeBron James appeared to be choosing among five contenders after he entered free agency: the Philadelphia 76ers, the Miami Heat, the Minnesota Timberwolves, the Denver Nuggets and the Cleveland Cavaliers.
James, in something of a surprise, picked the 76ers. And through the (very) early part of this season, he appears to have chosen wisely.

Philadelphia is 8-1 after a win over the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday night. The 76ers have the most wins in the NBA entering Friday, and their high-powered starting five has jelled quickly to form an undeniable title contender.
The starting five
In addition to signing James, Philly traded for swingman Jaylen Brown in the offseason, forming a starting five of James, Brown, Tyrese Maxey, V.J. Edgecombe and Joel Embiid.
Those five players have combined for 36 All-Star selections, five MVP awards and five Finals MVP awards. So it’s perhaps unsurprising the group has been great together on the floor.

In 77 minutes together across five games, the Sixers’ starting five has outscored opponents by 15 points. Philadelphia’s opening quintet is dominating defensively, holding opponents to only 95.4 points per 100 possessions. (For context, the league’s best defense entering Thursday was holding opponents to 103 points per 100 possessions.)

“Our defense is going to be our identity,” James said Wednesday after the win over the Pistons. “We have a lot of scoring. We know that from individuals. We’re still figuring out that side of the floor out on the offensive side. Defensively, that’s where we are going to make our mark.”

James has meshed well with all of his co-stars so far. All two-man lineups featuring a combo of James plus one of Maxey, Brown, Embiid and Edgecombe have outscored opponents through the team’s first nine games.

title: LIV Golf plans to shut down
summary: LIV said discussions with financial backer BC Partners failed to produce an agreement to keep the controversial league going.
story: LIV Golf, the breakaway golf tour backed by Saudi royalty and some of the biggest names in the game, said Thursday it planned to wind down — a stunning conclusion to an effort that had received billions of dollars in backing.
In a statement, LIV said discussions with financial backer BC Partners had failed to produce an agreement to keep the league going.
“In light of the current circumstances, we believe shifting toward an orderly wind-down is the most responsible path forward for the League at this time,” LIV said in the statement.

Formed in 2021 by a group of golfers led by Phil Mickleson and Greg Norman who expressed dissatisfaction with the long-running PGA Tour, LIV attracted numerous boldface names including Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson with millions in guaranteed payouts.
Since 2022, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, the league’s primary backer, has invested more than $5 billion.

Its creation set off a civil war of sorts in the game between LIV players and others committed to sticking with the PGA Tour, whose tournaments were seen as more competitive. By contrast, LIV’s events were accused of lacking drama because players’ payouts were guaranteed.
While LIV tournaments attracted healthy audiences overseas, they failed to land a long-term TV partner in the U.S., hampering their visibility and revenue streams.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
An earlier hearing in New Jersey bankruptcy court indicated LIV planned to shut down operations as it sought relief from creditors. It was not immediately clear how much it owed.

The Financial Times reported earlier this week that LIV had sought a last-minute investment with a large private equity group, only to see the deal fall apart. Sports media outlet The Athletic reported the group, BC Partners, did not receive enough commitments from golfers interested in reviving the tour, which had seen multiple events canceled this year, including a team championship.

title: Martha Stewart Sits Down With Craig Melvin to Address Halloween Costume Controversy
summary: During the Nov. 6 TODAY episode, Martha Stewart addressed the backlash she received following her controversial Halloween costume.
story: Martha Stewart apologized on TODAY following her controversial Halloween costume that appeared to depict a homeless person and said Craig Melvin was not at fault for her wearing the outfit that sparked a backlash.

The 85-year-old lifestyle guru has been facing criticism since she posted a now-deleted photo of her looking disheveled while holding a clipboard that read, “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!” for Halloween, per NBC News. During her appearance on TODAY Nov. 6, Stewart addressed the controversy and how Craig got roped into it.

“I made a mistake,” Stewart said. “I was stupid, what else can I say? I am so sorry, and I hope that my followers and my fans and the rest of America forgives me for doing something that was not meant in any way to be a bad thing.”

Craig then asked Stewart about reports that said she claimed she wore the last-minute costume because he spilled chocolate on her sweater during their TODAY Halloween special segment on Oct. 30, where Craig was dressed as rapper Snoop Dogg.
“I didn’t have a costume because you had spilled some chocolate on my white sweater, and I don’t blame you at all,” she told Craig. “It was a joke that I said I blamed you. It was stupid.”
Stewart said she was giving a talk and made a joke that Craig had spilled chocolate on her so she couldn’t wear that costume and pivoted to the other one instead.
“Of course, they picked up on that because you’re you,” Stewart said.
“But I did apologize for spilling the chocolate,” Craig said. “We moved on.”
“And it wasn’t your fault,” Stewart said.
She also shared feedback she received from her family.

“Tone-deaf, or whatever I was. According to my grandson, I was tone-deaf,” she said. “He saw the picture first because I sent it to him and I said, ‘What do you think?’ ‘Tone-deaf,’ he said. It was just stupid, and I apologize because I was not making fun of anybody or making light of the great problems that face our country.”
Stewart, who will return to TODAY next week for the annual All-Star Thanksgiving segment, shared what she learned from the controversy.
“Pay closer attention to social issues,” she said. “Be aware. I’m aware of all those social issues, as you can imagine, and I care desperately about all the problems facing us.”

For her Halloween costume, Stewart wore torn clothing and covered her face in makeup to resemble dirt. Her Instagram post with a picture of the costume doubled as an ad for her candle collection on QVC. “My QVC candles are perfect for Halloween!!!” she captioned the since-deleted post.
